solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Second chance to see trio, anyplace, anyhow

indicators.note: done anyhow means done in any old way, so these letters are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Three people wandering around randomly, anywhere at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports broadcast repeats a key moment so viewers get another look at it.

clue.text: Waylay coach, boarding in the morning, tailed by young officer briefly

indicators.note: tailed by means what follows comes after the earlier pieces

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks the morning hours
a coach you are boarding is a bus

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a cadet is an officer in training

explanation.surface: Someone is ambushed while getting on a morning coach, with a junior officer trailing behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boarding' looks like it puts one piece inside another, but the coach is simply the bus being boarded; 'briefly' drops the last letter of CADET.
explanation.definitionFit: To ambuscade is an archaic verb for lying in wait and attacking, just like an ambush.

clue.text: This swimmer fighting with cops could be spectator

indicators.note: fighting means jostling and mixed up together, so the letters combine and rearrange

parts.note: taken as written: its letters equal the answer plus those of cops
taken as written

explanation.surface: A little fish brawling alongside the police might turn out to be a mere onlooker.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer's letters together with COPS, shuffled ('fighting', 'could be'), make SPECTATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small, brightly coloured tropical freshwater fish popular in aquariums.

clue.text: Unpleasant task fetching up old gold

indicators.note: in a down clue, fetching up means lifting a letter to the top of the column

parts.note: a chore is a tedious or unpleasant job

explanation.surface: A disagreeable job digs up some ancient gold.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'up' is towards the top: the O of CHORE is brought to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellowish-brown earth pigment, so it names a golden colour.

clue.text: Settlement that could be an early one if put under pressure?

definitions.text: Settlement that could be an early one if put under pressure?

parts.words: Settlement that could be an early one if put under pressure?
parts.note: a debt settlement which a borrower might make ahead of schedule when a lender leans on them

explanation.surface: A debt settled ahead of time because the creditor was pushing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, putting the word under P (pressure) stacks P on top and makes the term for an early settlement; the whole clue also describes a debt paid back sooner when pushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying back borrowed money is a settlement of the debt, and lenders can demand it early.

clue.text: Bedgrudge standing in for a person on screen?

indicators.note: standing in means placed in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: per means for each, for a, as in 'ten pounds per head'
a misprint for begrudge, which means resent

explanation.surface: Bearing a grudge about replacing someone who appears on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing in for' reads as deputising, but 'for a' is the Latin-derived word meaning each, and 'standing in' places the grudge inside it. The clue as published has the typo 'Bedgrudge'.
explanation.definitionFit: A television host introduces the programme and appears in front of the camera.

clue.text: Isolated in flat, people with time to spare

indicators.note: to spare means given up, left out of the longer word

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
men means people

explanation.surface: Cut off in a flat, with folk who have hours on their hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set aside or separated from others means standing alone, cut off.

clue.text: Debate targets house undergoing renovation

indicators.note: a house being renovated is rebuilt and rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A discussion about which houses to pick for a refurbishment.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means to dispute a decision already made, so it is a kind of arguing.

clue.text: Disprove one posting videos online is making a comeback? Not you

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, read backwards
Not means the word that follows is left out

parts.note: a YouTuber posts videos on the website YouTube

explanation.surface: An online video maker staging a return, but it's not about you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not you' removes YOU, leaving TUBER, and 'making a comeback' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut is to refute an argument by contrary evidence.

clue.text: Dash it!

parts.note: an old-fashioned mild oath, read literally as an instruction to put a dash into a word

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a quaint curse; read as a command it tells you to join a compound with a short dash.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyphenating a compound word means joining its parts with a short line, a sort of dash.

clue.text: In revolutionary church, angry vigilantes like a preacher

indicators.note: In means the next piece sits inside the other
revolutionary means turned round, so the church letters read backwards

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: angry means agitated, so these letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Furious vigilantes in a church torn by revolution sound like a fiery sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' turns the church abbreviation round to EC, and the letters shuffled by 'angry' become VANGELISTI, which 'In' places between E and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelistic describes zealous gospel preaching aimed at converting people.

clue.text: Peacekeepers recklessly say help is out of proportion

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are the United Nations forces

indicators.note: recklessly means wildly, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers rashly asking for assistance makes things get out of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacking pleasing form or symmetry is badly proportioned, so ill-formed.

clue.text: Run more?

definitions.meaning: in cricket a bye or wide is a run not scored off the bat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Run more?' sounds like advice to a jogger; it is two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A run conceded not off the bat is a cricket bonus, and an additional amount is surplus.

clue.text: Change schools when one goes silent

indicators.note: goes means departs, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to school someone is to train them
I is the Roman numeral one
mute means silent

explanation.surface: Schools alter their ways when a pupil falls quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmute is to transform one thing into another, as alchemists hoped to with lead.

clue.text: Style of humour that could become racialist

indicators.note: could become means the letters may be turned into something else by rearranging

explanation.surface: Comedy that risks tipping into racism.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire is mocking humour that exposes folly, so this adjective describes that comic mode.

clue.text: Without pause announce a singer's engaged

indicators.note: engaged means held within, so the letters run inside these words

explanation.surface: Declaring that a vocalist has got engaged to be married.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never stops goes on continuously, endlessly.

clue.text: Band lisped musical number

indicators.note: spoken with a lisp, the S sound comes out as a TH

parts.note: a number in a musical is a song

explanation.surface: A group with a speech impediment performing a show tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' pretends to be a group of musicians; it is a strip of material.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of leather or cord used for fastening is a narrow band.

clue.text: Pop could get Oscar, having managed G. Depardieu on a regular basis

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ran means managed, as in running a business

indicators.note: on a regular basis means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A soft drink might win an Oscar after directing Gérard Depardieu now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters of DEPARDIEU taken are EADE, the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is British slang for a fizzy soft drink, and this is an orange-flavoured one.

clue.text: Incident, obvious, papers ignored

indicators.note: ignored means left out of the word

parts.note: evident means obvious
ID, identity documents, are papers

explanation.surface: An incident is plain to see, so nobody looked at the documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens, an occurrence, is an incident.

clue.text: Shriek from animal on a rock face, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is said and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: a cat (animal) beside 'a wall' (a sheer rock face), together CAT A WALL

explanation.surface: A screech from a creature clinging to a cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent 'cat-a-wall' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterwaul is a loud howling wail, like a cat in heat, so a scream.

clue.text: Happen to find ring caught by dog

indicators.note: by means next to, so the dog comes alongside

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Coming across a ring that a dog has snatched.
explanation.definitionFit: To occur is to take place or come about.

clue.text: Block narrow road

definitions.meaning: to block is to shut off
narrow here means tight or near, as in a narrow win
in Britain a ... is a short residential street, often a cul-de-sac

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: a verb, an adjective and a noun; read together they look like a lane obstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Shutting something off, a tight margin, and a dead-end street all share this one word.

clue.text: Joust between two adults good with just uncovered spears?

indicators.note: between means placed in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, twice
to spar is to fight or joust

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of the outside letters

explanation.surface: Two grown-ups tilting at each other with bare lances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spears' suggest lances in the joust; they are the edible shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: The young shoots of this vegetable are called spears.

clue.text: On opening, promoted communications device

indicators.note: promoted means raised, so in a down entry the letters read upwards

parts.note: re means on, concerning
a gap is an opening

explanation.surface: A gadget pushed up the rankings on the day it launched.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleeper that receives short messages is a communications gadget.

clue.text: Sticky stuff? Be naughty again

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to sin is to misbehave

explanation.surface: Something sticky prompts a child to misbehave once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one word, re-sin would mean to sin again, which is how the clue is built.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is the viscous sap that oozes from trees, so gooey material.

clue.text: Almost twenty, part of face finally getting hot

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, losing the last letter

parts.note: a score is twenty
the chin is part of the face

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Turning nearly twenty, and a person's face finally starts to burn.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorching weather is very hot, hot enough to burn.

clue.text: Lover briefly embraces married instructor

indicators.note: embraces means holds within its arms
briefly means shortened by the last letter

parts.note: a swain is a young lover or suitor

explanation.surface: A suitor briefly hugs the wedded teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu religious teacher is called a swami, so a spiritual guide.

clue.text: Anger shown by celeb upset about cross opponents

indicators.note: about means going round the other piece
upset means knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: a liger is a cross between a lion and a tigress
in bridge East and North are opposing players, E and N

explanation.surface: A disturbed celebrity fumes at cross rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' rearranges the celebrity into BELCE, which goes 'about' the rest. 'Cross' looks like a mood, but it is a lion-tiger hybrid; bridge partners sit opposite, so East and North oppose.
explanation.definitionFit: Belligerence is aggressive hostility, a fighting temper.
